page: Amazon Web Services c5d.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance offering direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead. It is powered by dual Intel Xeon 8275CL processors running at 3.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading. The system features 35 MB of L3 cache, 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, 3600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluation shows substantial multi-core compute and data-processing capabilities. The server demonstrates strong results in the top 25 percent tier for multi-core stress-ng workloads, PassMark CPU testing, PassMark database operations, Clang software compilation, and ray tracing. Memory throughput is also strong, achieving 236.4 GB/sec for uncached read operations. It delivers notable throughput in network- and storage-bound scenarios, such as 48.79 GB/sec in static web serving and 83.23 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including single-core Geekbench and compression tasks, sit within the middle 50 percent.

Given its bare-metal architecture, high vCPU density, and 3600 GB of low-latency NVMe instance storage, c5d.metal is well-suited for high-throughput batch processing, extensive CI/CD build farms, and distributed in-memory or transactional database workloads. However, without dedicated GPU acceleration, CPU-based LLM text generation throughput drops into the lower percentiles, making it inefficient for modern large-model generative AI serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.metal is a compute-optimized bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 8275CL processors on x86_64 architecture, featuring 48 physical cores, 96 dedicated vCPUs at 3.6 GHz, and 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It integrates 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without GPU accelerators. The instance demonstrates strong multi-core processing in stress-ng and PassMark benchmarks, alongside high-throughput metrics in software compilation, Redis operations (83.23 million ops/sec), and static web serving (48.79 GB/sec). While single-core performance and CPU-based LLM generation remain average to poor, the high core count and fast local NVMe storage deliver significant density and throughput for large-scale CI/CD pipelines, distributed databases, caching layers, and high-concurrency batch computation.
